answer: Each agent must back its identity with a fresh handwritten phrase captured on a digitizer, where pen pressure, stroke order and speed form a behavioral profile unique to one person. A registry rejects any profile too close to an existing one, so a single human can sustain only one identity however many agents they run. Forging distinct profiles at scale means hiring many writers or building a costly synthesis rig, while the check needs a digitizer, a human in the loop, and private stroke data: a glacier carves one path through rock, an ocean hides a single black onyx pebble among millions.
